chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Ali ibn Isma'il from Hammad ibn Isa from al-Husayn ibn al-Mukhtar from al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) who said:
One of you says, 'I am a stranger/guest,' but the true stranger is the one who is in the house of polytheism (dar al-shirk).

key_terms.إِنَّمَا: Indeed/Only; used to restrict or define the true meaning of a term.
key_terms.دَارِ الشِّرْكِ: House of polytheism; a metaphorical realm of disbelief or associating partners with God.
key_terms.غَرِيبٌ: Stranger or guest; one who is away from their homeland or home.

ai.seo_question: What is the true meaning of being a 'stranger' (gharib) in Shia theology according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) redefines spiritual alienation, asserting that true 'strangeness' is not physical displacement but residing in the 'house of shirk' (polytheism/disbelief). This reflects the Shia emphasis on *ghurba* as a state of being a stranger to the world due to adherence to divine truth amidst prevailing falsehood, a concept deeply rooted in the Ahl al-Bayt's experience. It serves as a reminder that spiritual belonging to God is paramount over geographical or social location.
